findings.evidence: Phase 2's terminal-versus-recoverable final-message rules, and the same warning order restated in phase 5 and phase 6, stay in a 462-line command after the body templates, assembly code and diagram filter were already split to skills/pr-diagrams/references/pr-body.md.
findings.fix: Move the final-message ordering (terminal failures begin with the tool stderr or named guard error; recoverable fallbacks begin with one warning line, then the outcome) into skills/pr-diagrams/references/pr-body.md and leave one sentence in phases 2 and 6 that says when to load that section.

findings.evidence: Phase 3 step 5 says reviewers are read only on a reuse path, while phase 5 says 'On success, do not run a second gh pr edit of the title or body' and 'A feature PR has no reviewer list, so it has no second gh pr edit.' The no-second-edit rule is already stated, and the feature-PR sentence adds nothing the model would miss.
findings.fix: Keep the phase 3 reuse-path condition and the phase 5 rule that a successful create is not followed by a title or body edit. Delete the feature-PR sentence and add a row for it to docs/audit/recovery/explain-pr-changes/record.md.

findings.evidence: Phase 4 says the mode is attach only when capability printed exactly attach and exited 0, and that empty output, any other output or a non-zero exit means branch. skills/pr-diagrams/scripts/pr-diagrams.sh cmd_capability always prints attach or branch and returns 0 for a valid probe, including when PR_DIAGRAMS_MODE is unset, and its help text says capability always exits 0. A non-zero exit is a usage error with empty stdout, so the branch fallback never matches a real capability result.
findings.fix: Treat stdout of exactly attach as attach and exactly branch as branch. If capability exits non-zero, stop before render and quote its stderr, the same way a failed related read stops, instead of calling that result branch mode.

findings.evidence: The head == base guard says to derive <short-slug> from the head name or the latest commit subject, with no default and no character rule, then run git switch -c "pr/<short-slug>". A subject can contain spaces, slashes or quotes, so the branch name is a guess on a step that creates a branch.
findings.fix: Default to a slug of the latest commit subject: lowercase, drop characters outside a-z, 0-9 and hyphens, collapse repeated hyphens, and cut at 40 characters. Use the head name only when the subject slug is empty.

findings.evidence: Section 2.2 says squash or rebase merges can pick an older cycle's PRs as sources, then stops unless every SRC entry is confirmed by git log --merges, but it never says how to tell a squash or rebase merge from a merge commit before that list is checked.
findings.fix: Add one Gotchas line: a squash or rebase merge has no merge commit, so git log --merges can list an older cycle's merges while the current cycle is absent; that partial list is the same stop as no merges.

findings.evidence: The description names the write action, the trigger phrases and the read-only neighbour, but it does not name the accepted argument tokens --diagrams, --reuse-from, --base or the bare aliases.
findings.fix: Create or update the GitHub pull request for the current branch from its committed diff: summary, changeset triage, optional Mermaid or draw.io diagram, promotion-branch bodies reused from merged PRs, and reviewers. Use when asked to open, write, refresh or describe a pull request, "explain PR changes", "open or refresh the PR summary", "promote develop to main", or "reuse merged PR bodies", including with --diagrams=none|mermaid|drawio, --drawio, --mermaid, --no-diagrams, --reuse-from=<PR> or --base=<branch>. Pushes feature branches and writes PRs. Not for a read-only explanation of a diff (use explain-changes-mental-model).
